Hey there- 
International travelers, first-time visitors to the U.S., families and small groups often enjoy staying in our apartment. 
About me: Professionally, I'm a producer/writer/journalist...and love learning about new people, things and places. Curiosity is an innate quality! I've traveled many places in the world and want to do more and more of it. 

The apartment is very large, in fact by NYC standards it is huge, and each of the 3 bedrooms has empty space for guests to store belongings (meaning the rooms are “guest ready” and not cramped with our personal items).

As for our location, I enjoy living in Harlem, which is in upper Manhattan, because it has a warm, energetic vibe. We are right on top of Central Park, about a 7 minute walk away. The apt is located in the southwest portion of Harlem, which has undergone extensive gentrification. The apt is close to many great subway lines that can take you anywhere in the city (to Times Sq in 2 stops off the express A and D lines...and to Brooklyn, Queens as needed).  The people in this neighborhood are friendly...ethnically diverse (as most of New York City is diverse!) You really could do well to take a moment to enjoy it up here :) also, the apt is located on a wide “quieter” Avenue (again by NYC standards) so you won't have all the crazy hustle and bustle and non-stop noise like the Times Sq area. 

We also have many new and great places to eat, grab a drink, listen to jazz (Minton’s is a 2-minute walk away!), go for coffee at Double Dutch and so on. Just outside your front door, you can walk steps to reach “restaurant row” on Frederick Douglass Blvd. You walk 1 minute to Best Market (currently being remodeled but Whole Foods is very close as is CTown Grocery), a 24-hour laundry, newer bars like Mess Hall and Harlem Tavern, cafes/restaurants like Vinateria, Lido, Harlem Burger, Row House, Levain Bakery’s famous cookies,, Lolo’s Seafood and more! You also are a 90 second walk away from the best local coffee shop called Double Dutch that offers a typical comfy NYC experience with great WiFi (there’s also a Starbucks across the street) and we are a 10 minute walk to Columbia University. *Whole Foods is walkable in the other direction in less than 10 minutes as well.

There are hip restaurants walking distance in Bed Stuy, or 1 subway stop or short bus ride away on Nostrand and Franklin Avenues.

Hey guys! My name is Jose David,  I am originally from El Salvador and came to the US at the age of 9. I grew up in Maryland and at the age of 18 I packed my bags, bought a one way bus ticket to New York and made this crazy beautiful city my home. 

On July 2020, After getting laid off  by the company I worked with, I decided to pause a very rewarding 17 year retail management career, and venture into the world of small business ownership. I have to say, this has been the most challenging and life changing decision I’ve ever had to make, and if I had to do it again, I wouldn’t change a thing. Every situation, whether good or bad,  and every obstacle I’ve faced thus far, has been a learning experience I wouldn’t change for the world. I became a business owner and opened a Barbershop in times of  COVID19 on September 2020. I knew I needed a change, so I was determined to overcome any challenge that came my way and not be deterred by the pandemic from pursuing my goals. So, as risky and crazy as it sounds to open a business during one of the worst financial crisis in the history of this beautiful nation, I wholeheartedly felt it was the right time. So boys, if you stay with me, you would not only have a barbershop 7 blocks away if you needed grooming services, but you’d also have an in house barber! Haha. I joined the Airbnb hosting community 5 years ago and since then, I have been a "Super Host" for over 4 years combined. I enjoy meeting people from all over the world, all walks of life, and learn  about their experiences, while hopefully creating new ones during their stay with me. that's why I host.  

I am respectful of my guests and go with the flow when it comes to communication and day to day interactions between us. The house is clean, quiet and I’d like to think it's relaxing and peaceful. I’m super laid back so If you have any questions about my place, the neighborhood or myself, feel free to ask! I'll gladly provide you with any information you require.

Brooklyn is New York's largest, most diverse and creative borough. Our neighborhood of Sunset Park is in South Brooklyn, near the waterfront. The apartment is three blocks from the park itself, the highest residential point in Brooklyn with panoramic views of Manhattan and the Statue of Liberty. The park has an Olympic size public swimming pool which is open and free of charge during the warm months.

Dylana is committed to undoing racism and believes that income sharing is one of the most promising leverage points for unlearning capitalist ideals, and practicing how to build new systems together. She dreams of having an income sharing co-op of 6 to 10 people who are part of a vast network of other income sharing co-ops that work together to build and share autonomous resources, and create long-term socially engaged art projects, initiatives, and political campaigns that dismantle unjust systems. She is particularly interested in shutting down factory farms and prisons, facilitating youth councils, creating alternatives to calling the police, developing software that supports cooperative operations, and figuring out where the money to start new co-ops is going to come from. For now, she is focused on providing support to our community, teaching others what she knows, curating events and installations that elevate public spaces outside of the mundane, managing our studio residencies, caring for street kitties, cooking, styling looks, and building relationships. host_about: Dylana co-founded GG’s because we need more community spaces where we can connect, support, and be accountable to each other. Through her participation in organizations like La Tabacalera, Este es Una Plaza, and Asemblea Lavapies in Madrid, Occupy Sandy and Flux Factory in NYC, European Dissent in New Orleans, and Round Sky Solutions in Vermont, as well as her research into intentional communities like Matavenero, Tamera, Twin Oaks, Acorn, and Compersia, she has learned what it really takes to share power and she is excited to share this experience with others. Dylana is committed to undoing racism and believes that income sharing is one of the most promising leverage points for unlearning capitalist ideals, and practicing how to build new systems together. She dreams of having an income sharing co-op of 6 to 10 people who are part of a vast network of other income sharing co-ops that work together to build and share autonomous resources, and create long-term socially engaged art projects, initiatives, and political campaigns that dismantle unjust systems. She is particularly interested in shutting down factory farms and prisons, facilitating youth councils, creating alternatives to calling the police, developing software that supports cooperative operations, and figuring out where the money to start new co-ops is going to come from. For now, she is focused on providing support to our community, teaching others what she knows, curating events and installations that elevate public spaces outside of the mundane, managing our studio residencies, caring for street kitties, cooking, styling looks, and building relationships. She's super busy but open to hanging out if the timing works!

neighborhood_overview:
Brooklyn Heights is a romantic step into New York's past. Its leafy streets, abundant historic buildings, classy restaurants and the expanding Brooklyn Bridge Park make it a wonderful place to get the quintessential New York vibe that is all but lost in Manhattan and Brooklyn.

The area was also where wealthy Wall Street families in the 19th century had their summer houses! The neighborhood was rapidly developed when the first elevated train was built shortly after 1900; the architecture is exceptionally coherent for New York City, almost all art déco, and most buildings are only 4–6 stories high.
